Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 26-year-old female with new, severe, right-eye-predominant headache with photophobia, visual aura, nausea, family history of migraine, no red-flag neurological signs.

Working diagnosis: Suspected migraine (possibly with aura).

Differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx):
• Migraine with aura – High likelihood given unilateral severe pain, photophobia, visual phenomena, nausea, strong family history.  
• Tension-type headache – Moderate likelihood; diffuse dull component and occupational strain but photophobia/aura less typical.  
• Acute sinusitis – Low–moderate; peri-orbital pain but lacks nasal/fever features.

Red-flag conditions (very low likelihood but counselled): meningitis, subarachnoid hemorrhage—patient advised to return if vision changes, weakness, worsening pain, fever, or vomiting.

Management Plan

• Educated on maximum safe dosing of ibuprofen (up to two 200-400 mg tablets three times daily with food).  
• Prescription offered for stronger analgesia: Naproxen and optional combination paracetamol/codeine (exact script details not documented).  
• Advised addition of paracetamol as needed.  
• Headache diary recommended to identify triggers and frequency.  
• Discussed possible prophylactic therapy if headaches recur; to reassess at follow-up.  
• Safety-net advice: return or call sooner for escalating headache, neurological deficits, vision loss, or systemic symptoms.  
• Suggested scheduling an optometry review due to longstanding glasses use and current visual strain.  
• Follow-up appointment arranged in 1–2 weeks.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Migraine (with or without aura) – High: Matches unilateral severe pain, photophobia, visual aura, nausea, and family history.  
2. Tension-type headache – Moderate: Diffuse dull component, work stress, screen use; less consistent photophobia.  
3. Acute sinusitis – Low–Moderate: Right peri-orbital pain and gradual onset; lacks sinus symptoms.
